Rishi — thanks for the demo yesterday. Procurement and legal had a couple of key concerns before we can move to an order form: primarily around whether ProspectCo retains ownership of model outputs and whether Redwood can use our inputs/outputs for training.

High level asks:
- Confirmation that all outputs generated by ProspectCo prompts will be owned by ProspectCo (or licensed to us for internal use, as applicable).

- If Redwood requests feedback/use of anonymized logs for product improvement, we need a narrow, time-boxed license and the ability to opt out.

We received the MSA shared during the call. Can you send suggested redlines or a short summary of how Redwood proposes to carve these items out in the Order Form? We need something we can run by our counsel this week.

Summary of proposed positions (short):
- Output ownership: ProspectCo retains ownership of outputs produced by your prompts. Redwood grants a limited service license to display, transmit, and temporarily store outputs solely to provide the service and for troubleshooting.
- Training/data use: Redwood will not use ProspectCo inputs/outputs to train or improve models unless ProspectCo provides an explicit opt-in at the customer or dataset level.
- Feedback/telemetry: Redwood requests a narrow, non-exclusive, revocable license to use de-identified, aggregated telemetry and feedback to improve service quality. We propose a 12-month retention window and an opt-out option per deployment.
- Emergency operational use: in the unlikely event of safety incidents we may access specific logs under an agreed process (notice + limited scope).

Subject: RE: Data use and IP questions for MSA/Order Form

Rishi — quick draft language below you can paste into the order form / MSA excerpt for ProspectCo counsel. Kept it narrow and operational to reduce escalation.

--- suggested excerpt (MSA / Order Form) ---
1) Customer Outputs. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the MSA, Customer shall retain all right, title and interest in and to any content, outputs, or artifacts generated by the Service in response to Customer prompts ("Customer Outputs"). Redwood is granted a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to store, cache, transmit and display Customer Outputs solely as necessary to provide the Service and for routine diagnostics. Redwood shall not assert any ownership rights in Customer Outputs.

2) Data for Model Training. Redwood will not use Customer Inputs or Customer Outputs to train, tune, or improve any models (including foundation models) unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in that (a) identifies the data to be used, (b) specifies the permitted use, and (c) permits Customer to revoke consent.

3) Telemetry & Feedback. Customer may elect to allow Redwood to collect de-identified and aggregated telemetry ("Telemetry") for service improvement. Telemetry shall exclude any Customer Outputs or Inputs that contain Personal Data or Customer Confidential Information. Telemetry use is subject to Customer's right to opt out at any time and will be retained for no longer than twelve (12) months unless otherwise agreed in writing.

4) Emergency Access. Redwood may access specific logs for resolution of a security or safety incident only upon notice to the Customer's security contact and limited to the minimum data necessary; such access is subject to audit and expiry.

--- end excerpt ---

A couple of negotiation tips for you: make the opt-in granular (per dataset or project) rather than a catch-all, and push for an explicit revocation mechanism in the Order Form UI/portal. If ProspectCo insists on a prohibition plus a carve-in for aggregated telemetry, the above should be an acceptable compromise. I also recommend we offer a two-week trial of data redaction/configuration to show how opt-out can be implemented without breaking product metrics.

Let me know if you'd like me to call Sarah directly.

Laura Bennett
Senior Sales Counsel, Redwood Inference
